tldr: Still no new trading session since Friday 20 Nov's close (Japan is on a bank holiday today; HK/SG/US have not opened yet), but Sunday brought the first organized pushback to the crash narrative: Treasury Secretary Bessent broke from the hawkish Fed chorus, warning the Fed risks overtightening -- traders are reportedly paring back odds of a 50bp December 'shock' hike in response.

China and Taiwan moved overnight to defend their markets: China cut margin requirements to 80% (from 100%, effective Nov 30) and floated a ChiNext market-maker mechanism after ~$1.7tn was wiped off Chinese tech; Taiwan banned short sales below the prior close and is actively deploying its NT$500bn stabilization fund after the TAIEX's worst week in 35 years. Targeted liquidity support, not a fix for the underlying AI-capex-credibility problem.

The Nvidia SEC-probe story narrowed overnight to a specific, more durable thread: reports now say it centers on a 2025 accounting change that obscured how much Nvidia revenue flows through Singapore entities, including Megaspeed -- a new Singapore-adjacent angle worth watching, distinct from the broader chip-diversion scandal.

Biggest risk to the book, unchanged: the ~2.49x-levered silver position remains FAILING its survivability metric. Credit markets confirm this is genuine, not sentiment-only, risk-off -- high-yield spreads widened +29bp this week to 352bp with CCC spreads above 1000bp over Treasuries (AI-linked credit distressed), while investment-grade spreads barely moved (+5bp) -- stress is real but still concentrated at the bottom of the credit stack, not yet systemic.

A fresh Strait of Hormuz tanker-military incident Sunday evening keeps a live geopolitical oil/safe-haven premium in play heading into Monday's Asia open -- UKMTO now counts the highest rate of shipping attacks there since the conflict began.

Macro regime re-verified today: direction unchanged (hawkish-Fed-into-AI-capex-unwind, riskOnProb 0.30) but now explicitly weighs Bessent's dovish counter-voice and the China/Taiwan stabilization measures against Friday's shock, rather than assuming straight-line deterioration.

regime.label: Hawkish Fed into AI-capex unwind / credit-stress risk-off, now with a dovish counter-voice and state-level stabilization measures
regime.oneLiner: Friday's crash hasn't reversed, but Sunday brought the first organized pushback -- Bessent on the Fed, Beijing and Taipei on their own markets -- even as widening high-yield credit spreads confirm the underlying stress is real.

topNews.headline: Nvidia SEC probe reportedly narrows to accounting/revenue-geography disclosures tied to Singapore entities
topNews.actionable: Adds a Singapore-specific thread to the Megaspeed scandal, raising the chance of follow-on MAS/exchange scrutiny of Singapore-domiciled tech entities -- a reputational tail-risk to watch rather than a direct holding issue.

topNews.headline: China eases margin rules, cuts trading fees, floats ChiNext market-maker system to stem $1.7tn tech selloff
topNews.actionable: A modest, targeted liquidity tailwind for HK-listed China tech (0700.HK/0981.HK/1810.HK) into Monday's open, though it addresses market plumbing, not the underlying AI-capex-credibility overhang.

topNews.headline: Treasury Secretary Bessent breaks with hawkish Fed chorus, warns against overtightening
topNews.actionable: If this pushback trims odds of a 50bp 'shock' hike at the Dec 8-9 FOMC, it's a tentative positive for the levered silver/miner book, which was hit hardest by hawkish repricing on Friday.

topNews.headline: Taiwan widens short-sale ban and deploys NT$500bn stabilization fund after TAIEX's worst weekly drop in 35 years
topNews.actionable: State intervention in the Taiwan tech/semi complex may put a floor under the AI-supply-chain selloff, a modest sentiment offset for correlated HK/China semis exposure -- though the scale of the response signals how severe the damage is.

topNews.headline: Strait of Hormuz shipping attacks hit highest level since the conflict began; fresh tanker-military incident Sunday evening
topNews.actionable: A live geopolitical oil/safe-haven tail risk heading into Monday's open -- worth watching given the portfolio's large cash pile and precious-metals tilt.

signals: HYG/credit spreads: HY OAS widened +29bp this week to 352bp with CCC spreads above 1000bp over Treasuries (AI-linked credit distressed) while IG spreads barely moved (+5bp) -- consider watching high-yield, not just the VIX, as the real-time confirmation of whether this risk-off is genuine or sentiment-only.

Rare-earth basket (MP/USAR/REMX/REXC): China's export-control truce extension to Jan 10 2027 removes the near-term scarcity catalyst that had driven Nov 13-19's 2-8% rally -- watch whether the structural DoD-backed thesis (MP's magnet offtake, USAR's CHIPS funding) reasserts once that near-term pop fades.

Defensive-sector rotation (XLP/XLU/XLV): the trio has outperformed Nasdaq100 by roughly 23pp since Oct 1 -- worth watching for continuation into Monday's Asia/US open as a read on whether the rotation out of AI/growth persists or fades post-options-expiry.

Crypto risk gradient: BTC<ETH<SOL in this drawdown (SOL down ~30% in November alone, broke its 200-day average) -- a read on risk appetite worth monitoring rather than a reason to add or trim any single name.

COPX/copper: record Chinese physical premiums (~$350-500/tonne, from under $100 in September) against a paper price down more than 9% this week -- a physical/paper divergence worth watching for mean-reversion once forced selling clears, echoing the same dynamic already flagged in silver.
